nodes.title: Every Hero Starts Somewhere
nodes.summary: MC accepts a routine wild-boar request from Primora's local guild post, showing an earnest desire to become a hero without grand destiny or prophecy.

beats.title: A Small Request
beats.screenAction: MC accepts a low-risk wild-boar request at Primora's guild post before leaving for the nearby forest.
beats.dialogueIntent: Establish MC's hero aspiration lightly and quickly; keep village life ordinary.
beats.result: MC leaves Primora carrying the ordinary starting sword and a routine request.

script.text: Morning light settles over Primora Village. A small request board stands beside the guild post.
Wild boar. North trail. That's it?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Try not to sound disappointed. Most people like easy work.
script.speaker: Guild Clerk

script.text: Every hero has to start somewhere.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: The clerk gives MC a look that is more amused than convinced.
Then start by coming back in one piece.
script.speaker: Guild Clerk

script.text: Player receives the routine wild-boar request and leaves Primora with the starting sword.
PRO-B01 — A Simple Hunt.

nodes.title: A Simple Hunt
nodes.summary: A routine wild-boar request teaches basic movement and sword combat before an abnormal threat interrupts the hunt.

beats.title: Routine Work
beats.screenAction: MC handles the expected low-threat target until a much heavier presence enters the area.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep the first fight simple and ordinary so the later chimera feels genuinely wrong.
beats.result: The ordinary tutorial threat is resolved and the anomalous creature interrupts the hunt.

script.text: Tutorial battle begins. Teach movement and the basic sword attack against an ordinary wild boar.
The boar circles through brush and charges.
Come on. I've handled worse training dummies than you.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: MC drives the boar off the trail and regains control of the clearing.
A heavier impact sounds deeper in the forest. Birds scatter.
...That wasn't the boar.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: The tutorial objective clears, but something much larger pushes through the trees.
PRO-B02 — The Wrong Beast.

nodes.title: The Wrong Beast
nodes.summary: The failed chimera breaks MC's starting sword and injures MC. The encounter becomes an escape sequence ending in an accidental crossing through a small Fracture.

beats.title: The Wrong Target
beats.screenAction: The anomalous chimera appears. MC attacks, the creature intercepts the strike, breaks the sword, and throws MC back.
beats.dialogueIntent: Destroy MC's confidence quickly; the creature behaves as a dangerous physical threat, not a speaking villain.
beats.result: MC is injured, the sword is broken, and direct fighting is no longer viable.

script.text: A failed chimera forces its way between the trees: bear-like body, four powerful forelimbs, and a bull-like head.
...That's not a boar.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Objective: Assess the threat. MC still has normal Attack.
MC steps in and commits to a sword strike.
The creature intercepts the blade with brutal force.
The starting sword snaps. MC is hurled backward and hits the ground.
...Okay.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Running sounds good.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Escape
beats.screenAction: MC flees through the forest while injured and attack-limited, then tumbles through a visible refractive Fracture by accident.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep the escape immediate. Do not explain the Fracture, chimera origin, or destination selection.
beats.result: MC crosses the Fracture with clothing and carried gear; the destination remains unknown.

script.text: Objective changes to ESCAPE. Normal Attack is disabled; movement and route interaction remain available.
MC runs through the forest while the chimera pursues as an aggressive predator.
Branches tear at MC's clothes. Blood runs from the arm and forehead.
The ground drops sharply ahead. MC slips, tumbles down the slope, and sees a strange refractive shimmer between the trees.
What is—
script.speaker: MC

script.text: MC rolls through the distortion before there is time to stop.
The forest vanishes in a wash of bent light.
CH01-N01 — The Other Side.

nodes.title: The Other Side
nodes.summary: MC emerges from the Fracture injured and disoriented, is found by civilians/local escorts traveling with Julie d’Aubigny, receives Julie's practical aid, learns that Primora and Vaelkrath are unknown, and joins the group before road danger escalates into CH01-B01.

beats.title: Fracture Arrival
beats.screenAction: MC crashes into unfamiliar wooded farmland, still injured and carrying the broken starting sword. The small Fracture collapses without obvious trace.
beats.dialogueIntent: Pain and disorientation only; no cosmology explanation.
beats.result: MC is conscious, mobile, and still unable to make normal attacks.

script.text: A sharp shimmer folds in on itself behind MC and vanishes.
MC hits the ground hard and lies still for a moment.
MC pushes up, sees blood on one arm, then looks at the broken sword.
Still broken. Great.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Toward the Road
beats.screenAction: MC moves toward a nearby road after hearing a cart beyond the trees.
beats.dialogueIntent: MC assumes this is some unfamiliar region reached during the fall, not another world.
beats.result: A traveling group becomes audible and visible.

script.text: Player regains movement control. MC can move but cannot use a normal attack.
A cart wheel creaks beyond the trees.
People?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: MC heads toward the road, favoring the injured arm.

beats.title: The Group Finds MC
beats.screenAction: A small civilian/local-escort group finds MC. Julie is already traveling with them and notices the injuries.
beats.dialogueIntent: Caution from the escort; Julie's attention goes immediately to the visible injury.
beats.result: Julie becomes the first notable France character to take direct interest in MC.

script.text: The cart slows. One escort steps forward while the civilians keep their distance.
Stop there.
script.speaker: Local escort

script.text: I'm not looking for trouble.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Then put the sword down.
script.speaker: Local escort

script.text: MC looks at the broken blade.
This?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: A young woman notices the blood on MC's sleeve and forehead.
They're hurt.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: Julie Helps
beats.screenAction: Julie steps past the escort, checks MC's arm, and directs immediate aid before asking for an explanation.
beats.dialogueIntent: Practical compassion with restrained humor; no dramatic rescue speech.
beats.result: Julie personally helps MC despite not knowing who MC is.

script.text: The young woman kneels beside MC and holds out a hand.
Give me your arm.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: I'm fine.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: You're terrible at lying.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Can you move your fingers?
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Yeah.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Good. Keep it still.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: We still don't know who they are.
script.speaker: Local escort

script.text: Then ask after they stop bleeding.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: ...Thank you.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: You can thank me when you stop swaying.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: Foreign Words
beats.screenAction: The introduction itself reveals that the group's speech sounds foreign even though its meaning reaches MC clearly.
beats.dialogueIntent: Show the language anomaly with one sharp contradiction rather than a long explanation.
beats.result: MC realizes mutual spoken understanding is happening despite genuinely different languages.

script.text: Name?
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: {{MC_NAME}}. I'm from Primora.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: The group trades blank looks. MC listens more carefully to the young woman's voice.
Wait... what language are you speaking?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: French.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: ...What's French?
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Primora and Vaelkrath
beats.screenAction: MC names Primora and Vaelkrath; nobody recognizes either place.
beats.dialogueIntent: The locals are genuinely unfamiliar; Julie does not ridicule or accuse MC.
beats.result: MC gets the first major contradiction while still resisting an impossible explanation.

script.text: Primora Village. Vaelkrath. Neither of those means anything to you?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Never heard of either.
script.speaker: Civilian

script.text: Nor me.
script.speaker: Local escort

script.text: I'm not saying you're lying.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Then where am I?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: East of Orléans.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: Orléans
beats.screenAction: The group resumes travel. Orléans and the siege are introduced only as practical local context.
beats.dialogueIntent: Give the player recognizable historical clues while keeping MC focused on location and survival.
beats.result: Orléans becomes the best nearby place to seek treatment, supplies, and answers.

script.text: The group starts moving again. MC walks beside the cart.
We're bound toward Orléans. Bad road for it, with the English around.
script.speaker: Civilian

script.text: English?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: MC looks from the unfamiliar clothes and banners to the road ahead.
I'm starting to think I'm very far from home.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Stay With Us
beats.screenAction: Julie gives her name and tells MC to stay with the group rather than wander off injured.
beats.dialogueIntent: Create a direct personal bond and a practical reason to travel together, not political allegiance.
beats.result: MC accepts temporary help and joins the group toward safer ground and Orléans.

script.text: I'm Julie.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: {{MC_NAME}}. Again, I suppose.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: I remembered.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: We're heading toward Orléans. If you're looking for answers, you'll have better luck there than bleeding beside the road.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Can you walk?
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Probably.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Not very convincing. Stay with us.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: All right. Until I figure this out.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Trouble Ahead
beats.screenAction: The lead escort detects armed movement ahead and halts the group.
beats.dialogueIntent: Immediate practical escalation into B01.
beats.result: Load CH01-B01 — Strangers on the Road.

script.text: The lead escort suddenly raises a hand. The cart stops.
Quiet.
script.speaker: Local escort

script.text: Armed voices carry from beyond the bend.
Julie shifts closer to the civilians and reaches for her sword.
Looks like your peaceful walk will have to wait.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: CH01-B01 — Strangers on the Road.

nodes.title: Strangers on the Road
nodes.summary: First mandatory France battle. Protect/escort the civilian group and supply cart from armed foragers/stragglers while MC remains attack-limited. Julie is already present; Hangaku Gozen and La Hire enter through the fight.

beats.title: Protect the Cart
beats.screenAction: Armed foragers/stragglers rush the road. Julie and the escorts form a defense while civilians pull behind the cart.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make the first France battle about protecting ordinary people rather than defeating every enemy.
beats.result: The group holds long enough to start moving civilians and supplies out of the kill zone.

script.text: Behind the cart! Move!
script.speaker: Local escort

script.text: Julie draws her sword and takes position between the attackers and the civilians.
Stay with the wounded and keep them moving.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Battle preview: MC can move, assist civilians, interact with the route/cart, and survive, but normal Attack remains disabled.
I can still help.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Then help them get clear.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: An Arrow From Nowhere
beats.screenAction: A civilian is nearly cut off. A precise ranged strike from an unknown warrior interrupts the attacker before she enters the line herself.
beats.dialogueIntent: Introduce Hangaku by decisive action, not biography. Keep her identity hidden until dialogue earns it.
beats.result: A capable unknown warrior joins the defense and stabilizes the road flank.

script.text: One attacker breaks past the escort and closes on a civilian.
A missile strikes the attacker's weapon arm and knocks the blow aside.
A composed warrior steps into the road between the civilian and the next attacker.
Behind me.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: She does not wait for thanks before turning back toward the threat.

beats.title: A Loud Reinforcement
beats.screenAction: Pressure builds on the opposite side until a rough-edged swordsman crashes into the attackers from the road.
beats.dialogueIntent: Contrast Hangaku's controlled entrance with La Hire's aggressive battlefield energy; keep his identity hidden until reveal.
beats.result: The attackers lose momentum and the civilians gain an escape route.

script.text: More armed men appear at the rear of the cart.
They're closing the road!
script.speaker: Local escort

script.text: A battered swordsman slams into the nearest attacker from the side.
You picked a damned poor road to rob today.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: He grins like the fight has finally improved his mood.

beats.title: Get Them Through
beats.screenAction: The improvised defenders create a corridor. MC focuses on getting civilians and the supply cart through while the others hold the attackers.
beats.dialogueIntent: Let MC contribute meaningfully without undoing the prologue defeat or attack limitation.
beats.result: Civilians and cart escape the immediate road threat.

script.text: Objective update: escort the civilians and cart through the open route.
MC braces one shoulder against the cart as a wheel catches in a rut.
Push!
script.speaker: MC

script.text: The cart breaks free while Julie, the unknown warrior, and the rough swordsman hold the road.
The group clears the ambush and reaches temporary shelter before nightfall.

beats.title: Names After Danger
beats.screenAction: Once the immediate danger passes, the two newcomers finally give their names.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep the introductions short; the battle itself should have already defined their first impressions.
beats.result: Hangaku Gozen and La Hire become known to MC; the group moves to shelter.

script.text: At the edge of shelter, Julie finally lowers her sword.
You have a name?
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Hangaku Gozen.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: La Hire.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: That sounded less like an introduction and more like a warning.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Good. You heard it properly.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: CH01-N03 — Shelter Before Nightfall.

nodes.title: Shelter Before Nightfall
nodes.summary: Post-B01 shelter, treatment, food and rest. MC builds early rapport with Julie, Hangaku and La Hire, then receives a cheap replacement sword after recovery.

beats.title: Food, Water, Bandages
beats.screenAction: At a rough shelter, Julie properly cleans and binds MC's injuries while the group eats and settles.
beats.dialogueIntent: Use recovery to let personalities breathe after the battle.
beats.result: MC is stable enough to rest and talk; the immediate road danger is behind them.

script.text: Julie tightens a clean wrap around MC's arm.
You were supposed to stay out of the fighting.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: I did.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: You ran directly toward three armed men.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: I said I didn't fight them.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Julie fails to hide a short laugh.

beats.title: Not the Only Stranger
beats.screenAction: MC asks Hangaku where she comes from and realizes another exceptional traveler may also be far from home.
beats.dialogueIntent: Hint at broader displacement without explaining Story Worlds or Fracture cosmology.
beats.result: MC gains reason to suspect the strangeness is larger than a simple wrong turn.

script.text: Hangaku... where are you from?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Far enough that most people here have never heard the name.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: So I'm not the only one.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Not the only one who is far from home.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: She leaves the rest unanswered.

beats.title: A Usable Sword
beats.screenAction: La Hire notices the broken sword and points MC toward a cheap replacement among available gear.
beats.dialogueIntent: The replacement is ordinary and practical; it matters because MC can carry a complete sword again, not because it is special.
beats.result: MC obtains a cheap replacement sword but remains hesitant to use it in real combat.

script.text: La Hire turns the broken starting sword over once and snorts.
You're carrying this?
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: It used to be better.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Most things did.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: He points to a plain, worn but serviceable sword among the spare gear.
Take that one. It won't impress anyone, but it won't fold in half either.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: MC takes the replacement sword and tests its weight without drawing it fully.
CH01-N04 — Names That Should Mean Nothing.

nodes.title: Names That Should Mean Nothing
nodes.summary: Recovery and context deepen the contradiction: France, England, Orléans and Charles/the Dauphin mean nothing to MC, while Primora and Vaelkrath mean nothing to the others. Orléans becomes the practical route toward answers.

beats.title: France
beats.screenAction: Simple conversation names France, England, Orléans, and Charles/the Dauphin. None of them belong in MC's known world.
beats.dialogueIntent: Turn necessary context into a growing contradiction, not a history lecture.
beats.result: MC can no longer comfortably explain the situation as merely being somewhere distant in Vaelkrath.

script.text: This is France?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Yes.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: And England is actually called England.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Usually.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: Orléans. France. England. Charles, the Dauphin... none of those names mean anything to you.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: Should they?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Nobody answers immediately.

beats.title: Where Is Vaelkrath?
beats.screenAction: Julie asks the question plainly: where is Vaelkrath supposed to be? MC realizes there is no map direction that can answer.
beats.dialogueIntent: Let MC reach fear and uncertainty before reaching a formal another-world conclusion.
beats.result: MC decides Orléans is the best route to information and a possible way home.

script.text: Where exactly did you say Vaelkrath was?
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: It's... everywhere. Primora is in Vaelkrath. The mountain road, the southern jungle, the coast—
script.speaker: MC

script.text: MC stops as the explanation becomes impossible to finish.
I need to get to Orléans.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: For what?
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Answers.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Good. We needed a reason to keep walking.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: Leave at First Light
beats.screenAction: The group prepares to continue toward Orléans with the civilians and supplies.
beats.dialogueIntent: End recovery cleanly and move back into danger.
beats.result: The party route is set toward Orléans.

script.text: By first light, the cart is repacked and the road group is ready to move.
MC straps the cheap replacement sword at the hip.
CH01-B02 — The Road to Orléans.

nodes.title: The Road to Orléans
nodes.summary: Combat climax against an organized English siege-line road detachment/outer screen. The group opens the cordon, frees detainees and escapes before reinforcements. MC restores basic Attack with the cheap replacement sword when protecting Julie from immediate danger.

beats.title: The Cordon
beats.screenAction: An organized English road detachment stops the group, controls passage, and begins inspecting supplies and travelers.
beats.dialogueIntent: Start with pressure and negotiation, not instant combat. Establish that simply walking away will strand or expose the civilians.
beats.result: The checkpoint blocks safe passage and begins detaining travelers.

script.text: A timber barrier and armed detachment block the road. Several travelers are already being held aside.
Cart stays. Names and business.
script.speaker: English Sergeant

script.text: Julie steps forward before La Hire can.
Civilians. Food. We want passage.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Then you'll wait while we decide what belongs to you.
script.speaker: English Sergeant

script.text: Two soldiers begin pulling a messenger and another traveler toward the guarded side of the road.

beats.title: Open the Road
beats.screenAction: The detention turns violent. La Hire and Hangaku act to open the cordon and free the people being held.
beats.dialogueIntent: Escalate from passage dispute to rescue/breakthrough. MC still hesitates to draw the replacement sword.
beats.result: The barrier is breached and detainees begin escaping.

script.text: Enough talking.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: La Hire knocks the first guard off the barrier while Hangaku moves to the detainees.
Objective: open the cordon and free detainees. MC can move and assist but does not yet use normal Attack.
MC reaches for the replacement sword, stops, and instead helps pull a detainee clear.
Move. Don't wait for us.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Reinforcements
beats.screenAction: The detachment signals for reinforcements, including a mounted enemy presence that makes the escape window narrow.
beats.dialogueIntent: Raise urgency and preview Cavalry pressure without turning this into a full siege battle.
beats.result: The objective changes from holding ground to escaping before the road is sealed again.

script.text: A horn sounds from the far side of the road.
More coming!
script.speaker: Local escort

script.text: Mounted soldiers appear beyond the checkpoint.
Objective update: escape before reinforcements close the route.
Don't hold the road. Break through and go!
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: Draw the Sword
beats.screenAction: An attacker slips through toward Julie while she is covering the retreat. MC reacts before thinking and finally draws the replacement sword.
beats.dialogueIntent: Pay off Julie helping MC in N01. The action is protective and instinctive, not a sudden cure for fear.
beats.result: MC regains basic Attack for the remainder of the battle preview.

script.text: Julie turns to shove a civilian toward the open route. An English soldier slips past the line behind her.
MC sees the raised weapon.
The replacement sword clears its sheath for the first time.
MC catches the incoming strike before it reaches Julie.
Basic Attack unlocked for MC in this draft battle intent.
Move!
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Julie meets MC's eyes for half a second, then turns back to the escape route.

beats.title: Breakthrough
beats.screenAction: The party and civilians complete the breakthrough before reinforcements can trap them.
beats.dialogueIntent: End on escape and survival, not annihilation of the English detachment.
beats.result: The road group escapes the outer screen and continues toward Orléans.

script.text: Final objective: reach the exit with the civilian group.
Hangaku covers the last detainees. La Hire forces the pursuing line to hesitate.
MC and Julie cross the final stretch with the cart behind them.
The group clears the checkpoint before the reinforcements can close the road.
CH01-N06 — The Maid Is Coming.

nodes.title: The Maid Is Coming
nodes.summary: Chapter resolution. Jeanne remains physically offscreen; conflicting rumors establish that the Maid is coming while MC continues toward Orléans seeking answers and a route home.

beats.title: After the Road
beats.screenAction: After the escape, Julie notices that MC finally used the replacement sword.
beats.dialogueIntent: Give the prologue defeat a small emotional echo without dumping backstory.
beats.result: Julie understands that MC's reluctance to fight came from something recent and frightening.

script.text: The group slows only after the road behind them is safely out of sight.
MC looks down at the cheap sword. The blade is still intact.
You can fight.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Apparently.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: You didn't seem very happy about it.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Last time I tried, it didn't go very well.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Julie lets the answer stand.

beats.title: The Maid
beats.screenAction: Passing travelers trade conflicting rumors about a young woman called the Maid who is expected toward Orléans.
beats.dialogueIntent: Jeanne remains offscreen. Present hope, doubt, and uncertainty rather than authoritative prophecy.
beats.result: The Maid becomes the chapter-ending hook without replacing MC's practical search for answers.

script.text: They say she's coming.
script.speaker: Traveler

script.text: The Maid?
script.speaker: Civilian

script.text: Another rumor.
script.speaker: Second Traveler

script.text: Maybe. Or maybe Orléans finally gets something worth believing in.
script.speaker: Traveler

script.text: Who's the Maid?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Depends who you ask.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: Toward Orléans
beats.screenAction: The group continues toward Orléans. MC still wants answers and a route home; the Maid rumor becomes the next major story hook.
beats.dialogueIntent: Close the chapter quietly and keep MC's motivation personal rather than political.
beats.result: Chapter 1 ends with the party moving toward Orléans and the coming siege story.

script.text: Julie looks toward the distant road.
Come on. Maybe Orléans has your answers.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: MC follows with the replacement sword at the hip.
CHAPTER 1 COMPLETE
Next: Chapter 2 — The Siege of Orléans.

nodes.title: Behind the Walls
nodes.summary: MC reaches Orléans as part of La Hire's road group, but remains an unranked outsider. The group is given practical work among supplies, wounded, and messengers while Dunois remains a distant command figure.

beats.title: Useful Hands
beats.screenAction: The road group enters a city under siege. La Hire reports briefly to Dunois while MC, Julie, and Hangaku are directed toward supply and casualty work rather than the command table.
beats.dialogueIntent: Establish social distance. Dunois notices the group only as people La Hire brought in; MC has no rank, invitation, or automatic access.
beats.result: MC is inside Orléans and useful, but still outside the command circle.

script.text: Orléans is loud with carts, bells, repairs, wounded soldiers, and people arguing over food.
This is what everyone was trying to reach?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: This is what is still standing.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: Across the square, Dunois takes La Hire's report without stopping the orders already leaving his hands.
Your road people can help the quartermasters. If they can carry, bind, count, or run messages, use them.
script.speaker: Jean de Dunois

script.text: He did not even ask who we are.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: He has a city to keep alive. Give him a reason to remember later.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: CH02-N02 — The Maid Enters Orléans.

nodes.title: The Maid Enters Orléans
nodes.summary: Jeanne enters Orléans as a distant public symbol. MC sees the city's hope gather around a tired young woman, then returns to ordinary siege work. Three local missions become available; any two may be completed in any order before higher command pays real attention.

beats.title: The Maid in the Crowd
beats.screenAction: Crowds gather around Jeanne's entry. MC catches only fragments of her through banners and people and never reaches her.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep Jeanne distant, human, and burdened by public hope. No private protagonist access yet.
beats.result: MC understands why the Maid rumor mattered, but Jeanne remains someone seen from the crowd.

script.text: A wave of shouting rolls down the street before MC can see its cause.
What happened?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: She made it into the city.
script.speaker: Civilian

script.text: A white banner rises above the crowd. Beneath it rides a young armored woman, visibly tired and trying to acknowledge everyone at once.
They look at her like the siege is already over.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: That is a dangerous amount of hope to put on one person.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

beats.title: Back to Ordinary Work
beats.screenAction: The crowd disperses and MC's group is sent back to the unglamorous work of a besieged city. Three unrelated local problems are posted at once.
beats.dialogueIntent: Turn the chapter from spectacle back to earned credibility. The party chooses where to help first rather than being summoned upward.
beats.result: The three free-order reputation missions unlock. Any two are sufficient to continue; the third remains optional.

script.text: The crowd closes. Jeanne disappears from view before MC gets anywhere near her.
By the time MC reaches the quartermaster yard again, nobody there cares about banners. Three different problems are waiting.
Couriers cut off east of the gate. A supply run under pressure. And an outer watch that stopped answering.
script.speaker: Quartermaster

script.text: Which one first?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Whichever keeps people alive. We can argue about the rest after.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Reputation missions unlocked: complete any 2 of 3 in any order. The remaining mission is optional after the threshold is reached.

nodes.title: The Cut Road
nodes.summary: Free-order reputation mission 1/3. Returning couriers and wounded soldiers are cut off on an outer approach. MC's group must reach them, cover the withdrawal, and return the dispatches. This is a Fantasia local siege incident, not a claimed historical battle.

beats.title: Find the Cut-Off Party
beats.screenAction: The obvious road is watched. MC identifies a lower farm track and guides the group toward the stranded couriers.
beats.dialogueIntent: First achievement should show judgment and initiative, not protagonist-level battlefield command.
beats.result: The party reaches the stranded couriers before the English screen closes around them.

script.text: Objective: reach the stranded party and secure the dispatch carrier.
The obvious road is watched. MC spots a lower farm track partly hidden by hedges and broken walls.
That way is ugly, but it is not covered.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Ugly is useful. Move.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

beats.title: Hold the Return Lane
beats.screenAction: English screen troops close from the main road while the wounded are moved. The party must hold a narrow return lane instead of chasing a victory.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make protection and discipline the achievement. The mission succeeds because people and dispatches escape.
beats.result: The wounded and dispatch carrier start moving while MC's group holds the pursuit back.

script.text: The group reaches the couriers as English screen troops begin closing from the main road.
Take the wounded first. We hold until they are moving.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Objective update: cover the withdrawal and keep the dispatch carrier moving.
MC holds the narrow return lane long enough for the last courier to clear it.

beats.title: Witnesses at the Gate
beats.screenAction: The recovered party returns through the gate with people and dispatches intact. Local witnesses now have a concrete story about MC's group.
beats.dialogueIntent: Close on reportable service rather than celebration. This is one independent reputation source, not enough by itself for command access.
beats.result: Reputation mission 1 is recorded. Another independent mission is still required for mandatory progression.

script.text: The party reaches the gate with people and dispatches intact.
We would have lost the dispatches without them.
script.speaker: Orléans Courier

script.text: Tell the quartermaster what happened. Not a better version of it.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: Reputation progress: 1 independent mission completed. Complete one more of the three to unlock the mandatory route.

nodes.title: Supplies Under Fire
nodes.summary: Free-order reputation mission 2/3. A supply train carrying food, bandages, and arrows is scattered under pressure. MC's group recovers the useful loads and escorts survivors back. This is a Fantasia local siege incident, not a claimed historical battle.

beats.title: Find What Still Moves
beats.screenAction: A damaged supply train is spread across a dangerous approach. The party must identify surviving drivers and salvageable loads before choosing a return route.
beats.dialogueIntent: Achievement two tests prioritization under pressure: save people and useful supplies instead of treating every enemy as the objective.
beats.result: Survivors and the most important loads are identified before the enemy closes.

script.text: Objective: locate surviving drivers and mark the food, bandage, and arrow carts that can still move.
Broken crates and frightened horses make the road look worse than the enemy numbers actually are.
We cannot take everything.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: Then we take what the city cannot replace first.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Move the Loads
beats.screenAction: The party forms a moving escort around the recovered wagons while skirmishers pressure the rear and flank.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make the second report about reliability: MC keeps the route moving rather than breaking formation for kills.
beats.result: The essential wagons and surviving drivers reach the safer lane toward Orléans.

script.text: Objective update: escort the marked wagons and surviving drivers to the gate route.
A driver freezes when arrows strike the road ahead. MC takes the bridle and keeps the wagon moving.
Do not stop for me. Keep the line moving!
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: The group refuses the easier chase and keeps the escort intact.

beats.title: The Quartermaster Counts
beats.screenAction: Back inside Orléans, the quartermaster counts recovered food, bandages, arrows, and living drivers rather than enemy bodies.
beats.dialogueIntent: Create an independent civilian/logistics report of competence. This can satisfy the second mandatory reputation source.
beats.result: Reputation mission 2 is recorded; if any other reputation mission is already complete, A Name Passed Upward unlocks.

script.text: The quartermaster checks the wagons twice before looking at the party.
Food, bandages, arrows, four drivers. Better than I expected.
script.speaker: Quartermaster

script.text: That sounded almost like praise.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Do not get used to it.
script.speaker: Quartermaster

script.text: Reputation progress updated. Mandatory route unlocks after any 2 of the 3 independent missions are complete.

nodes.title: The Outer Watch
nodes.summary: Free-order reputation mission 3/3. A local watch position stops answering after an English probe. MC's group reinforces the surviving watch, prevents a collapse, and creates a route back. This is a Fantasia local siege incident, not a claimed historical battle.

beats.title: A Silent Post
beats.screenAction: The party reaches a damaged watch position and finds a handful of defenders pinned rather than destroyed.
beats.dialogueIntent: Achievement three tests reading a bad situation quickly. The goal is to stabilize local defenders, not replace them as heroes.
beats.result: The surviving watch is contacted and a defensible route is identified.

script.text: Objective: reach the silent watch and locate surviving defenders.
The position looks abandoned until a hand rises behind a broken wall.
Five of us. Two hurt. They are waiting for us to run.
script.speaker: Watch Sergeant

script.text: Then we make the running part happen on our terms.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Hold, Then Break
beats.screenAction: The party helps the watch hold just long enough to move the wounded and then breaks contact through a safer route.
beats.dialogueIntent: Show restraint and coordination. MC's party enables the local soldiers to survive rather than taking over their post permanently.
beats.result: The defenders withdraw in order instead of being routed or trapped.

script.text: Objective update: hold until the wounded move, then break contact through the orchard lane.
Thirty breaths. Then we leave.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: MC counts the retreat by people rather than by defeated enemies.
Last one is moving. Go!
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: A Sergeant's Report
beats.screenAction: The watch sergeant reports that the outsiders reinforced the post, moved the wounded, and withdrew cleanly. La Hire hears the report separately from the other missions.
beats.dialogueIntent: This is a military witness independent of the courier and quartermaster accounts. If it is the second completed mission, the party has enough credibility to reach Dunois.
beats.result: Reputation mission 3 is recorded; if any other reputation mission is already complete, A Name Passed Upward unlocks.

script.text: They did not save the post. They saved the people in it.
script.speaker: Watch Sergeant

script.text: Good. Posts can be rebuilt.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: La Hire looks toward MC's group, then back to the sergeant instead of making a ceremony of it.
Reputation progress updated. Mandatory route unlocks after any 2 of the 3 independent missions are complete.

nodes.title: A Name Passed Upward
nodes.summary: After any two of the three local reputation missions, multiple independent reports reach higher command. La Hire confirms his own firsthand experience, and Dunois finally treats MC's party as useful irregulars worth assigning to Saint-Loup.

beats.title: Two Reports, Same Names
beats.screenAction: Reports from at least two unrelated local groups reach Dunois: couriers, quartermasters, or watch soldiers depending on the missions completed. La Hire confirms he already saw the party hold together on the eastern road.
beats.dialogueIntent: Recognition must come from repeated evidence. The exact completed mission pair may vary, but the common fact is that independent witnesses describe the same reliable group.
beats.result: Dunois now remembers the party as a proven irregular group rather than extra hands from La Hire's road column.

script.text: Two separate reports bearing the same unfamiliar names land on Dunois's table before La Hire enters.
Couriers, supply hands, the outer watch. Different problems. Same group keeps appearing in the reports.
script.speaker: Jean de Dunois

script.text: Same group I told you about from the eastern road.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: Dunois finally looks at MC long enough to match the name to the face.

beats.title: Work, Not Rank
beats.screenAction: Dunois assigns the party to the supporting line for Saint-Loup. The offer is practical work and responsibility, not a title or privileged place in command.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make the promotion social rather than formal: the party has become useful enough to receive real work and to be included in an operational briefing.
beats.result: MC's group earns a supporting assignment for Saint-Loup and is called to the crowded briefing where Jeanne is present.

script.text: I do not have ranks to hand out to strangers. I do have work for people who finish what they start.
script.speaker: Jean de Dunois

script.text: Work is fine. I still need answers when there is time.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Survive Saint-Loup first. Then remind me about your impossible map.
script.speaker: Jean de Dunois

script.text: The group is called to a crowded operational briefing because repeated service has earned it a place in the supporting line.

nodes.title: Beneath the Banner
nodes.summary: MC reaches Jeanne directly only after at least two independent local achievements, multiple reports, La Hire's confirmation, and Dunois's assignment. The meeting happens inside a crowded Saint-Loup briefing, not as a private audience or personal recruitment.

beats.title: A Place at the Edge of the Room
beats.screenAction: The party stands with other supporting groups at the edge of a crowded Saint-Loup briefing. Dunois names responsibilities; nobody treats MC as command staff.
beats.dialogueIntent: Show access as operational necessity. The party is present because Dunois assigned them after repeated reports.
beats.result: MC's party understands its limited supporting role and sees Jeanne working as one participant among commanders, messengers, and fighters.

script.text: The room is crowded with messengers and fighters, not arranged for a private audience. MC's group stands near the door with other supporting units.
The irregulars with the repeated local reports are with the supporting line. They answer to the field orders like everyone else.
script.speaker: Jean de Dunois

script.text: Bradamante checks her lance while Jeanne moves from one cluster of fighters to another instead of holding court.

beats.title: Jeanne the Person
beats.screenAction: Jeanne briefly speaks to MC's group while confirming the supporting line. She knows them from the reports, not because fate singled MC out.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make the first direct exchange practical and short. Jeanne is tired, direct, and human; MC remains socially junior.
beats.result: MC and Jeanne finally meet before fighting in the same operation; Bradamante is established for Saint-Loup.

script.text: You are the group from the road reports.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: Two of them, at least. Apparently that was enough to get us into this room.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Enough to trust you with work. That matters more than the room.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: She is pulled away by another messenger before the exchange can become anything grander.
Bradamante. Stay near my lane at Saint-Loup and we will both have fewer surprises.
script.speaker: Bradamante

script.text: CH02-B01 — Saint-Loup.

nodes.title: Saint-Loup
nodes.summary: The first major siege offensive. MC enters willingly as a functioning but still irregular fighter; the victory makes the group's usefulness public among the assault force.

beats.title: Under the Arrows
beats.screenAction: The Saint-Loup assault begins under missile pressure. MC's group works from the supporting line while established commanders direct the larger attack.
beats.dialogueIntent: Escalate clearly from local missions to a major siege assault without promoting MC into command.
beats.result: The supporting line crosses the exposed approach without bunching or collapsing.

script.text: Objective: cross the exposed approach and keep the supporting line intact.
Do not bunch under the arrows! Keep moving!
script.speaker: Jean de Dunois

script.text: La Hire draws pressure across the approach while Bradamante watches for a safer lane.

beats.title: The Breach Lane
beats.screenAction: Bradamante identifies a gap. MC's group helps widen and hold it long enough for more of the assault to pass.
beats.dialogueIntent: Give MC a meaningful contribution inside a larger battle: recognize and exploit an opening without becoming the person who wins Saint-Loup alone.
beats.result: The supporting force reaches the inner position and the English defense begins to fold.

script.text: There. That gap.
script.speaker: Bradamante

script.text: I see it.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: MC advances with the assault instead of being protected by it.
Objective update: hold the breach lane until the supporting line passes through.

beats.title: After the Position Breaks
beats.screenAction: Saint-Loup falls. Cheers begin, but the wounded immediately turn victory into work.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make this the battle that spreads MC's reputation beyond the local witnesses while immediately complicating the idea of glory.
beats.result: Saint-Loup is secured; soldiers beyond La Hire's immediate circle now recognize MC's group, and the aftermath leads into The Cost of Hope.

script.text: The position finally breaks. Cheers are cut short by the wounded being carried out.
Help them first. Celebrate when there is room.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: CH02-N05 — The Cost of Hope.

nodes.title: The Cost of Hope
nodes.summary: After Saint-Loup, recognition feels less glamorous up close. MC helps among the wounded, Jeanne escapes demands for certainty, and both confront the cost attached to being called useful or heroic.

beats.title: After the Cheering
beats.screenAction: MC carries water and supplies among casualties while soldiers who now recognize the party ask for help without ceremony.
beats.dialogueIntent: Recognition should feel like responsibility before it feels like prestige.
beats.result: MC feels the weight of becoming someone others expect to be useful.

script.text: MC stacks water beside the wounded long after the cheering from Saint-Loup has faded.
People know your name now.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: I liked it better when they did not.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Hope Still Has a Cost
beats.screenAction: Jeanne briefly joins the casualty work after escaping another round of officers and civilians demanding certainty.
beats.dialogueIntent: Build connection through shared labor and fatigue, not destiny or instant friendship.
beats.result: Jeanne and MC understand each other slightly better; the next operation feels chosen rather than automatic.

script.text: Jeanne arrives with the same exhausted expression after escaping another cluster of questions.
That part does not improve.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: Then why keep going?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Because the wounded are still here, and the siege is still here.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: MC hands another cup of water down the line before answering.
Fine. One problem at a time.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: CH02-B02 — Across the Loire / The Augustins.

nodes.title: Across the Loire / The Augustins
nodes.summary: The campaign shifts across the Loire. MC is now trusted to hold a real part of the operation, but still follows the established commanders rather than joining their rank.

beats.title: Establish the Crossing
beats.screenAction: The force begins crossing under pressure. MC's group is trusted with keeping one practical route open, not commanding the operation.
beats.dialogueIntent: Escalate from breach work to maintaining a vulnerable link between separated fronts.
beats.result: The first crossing lane remains usable long enough for the operation to spread across the river.

script.text: Objective: establish the crossing and keep the first route open.
If that crossing closes, half of us fight alone.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: Then we keep it open.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Separated Fronts
beats.screenAction: Pressure rises on both sides of the crossing. La Hire carries orders while MC's group absorbs pressure and keeps movement possible.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make coordination, not raw victory, the middle turn of the battle.
beats.result: The French maintain enough connection between fronts to push toward the Augustins.

script.text: La Hire carries orders between separated fronts while the supporting line absorbs pressure at the crossing.
Objective update: keep both fronts connected while the assault shifts toward the Augustins.
Do not chase. If the route breaks, we all pay for it.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: The Augustins Falls
beats.screenAction: After sustained fighting the Augustins position gives way, but the force is exhausted and cannot pretend the next assault will be easy.
beats.dialogueIntent: End with physical cost and the need for recovery before Tourelles rather than a clean victory montage.
beats.result: The Augustins falls. Exhaustion and casualties force a recovery beat before Tourelles.

script.text: After sustained fighting, the Augustins position gives way.
They are falling back toward the Tourelles.
script.speaker: Bradamante

script.text: And we are barely standing.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: CH02-N06 — Before the Tourelles.

nodes.title: Before the Tourelles
nodes.summary: The night before the siege climax slows the pace. The group treats wounds, argues about how far hope can carry exhausted people, and accepts that the next assault may be worse than anything so far.

beats.title: No Victory Lap
beats.screenAction: Weapons are repaired, bandages changed, and people sleep wherever they can. Jeanne wants to continue while others openly acknowledge exhaustion.
beats.dialogueIntent: Create friction and recovery before Tourelles. Nobody is fearless and no one gets to call exhaustion weakness.
beats.result: The group admits both the necessity and the cost of another assault.

script.text: The camp is quieter than a victory should be. People repair straps, wash blood from hands, and sleep wherever they can.
If we go again tomorrow, some of these people will not come back.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: If we stop now, the Tourelles still controls the crossing.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: Both things can be true.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: Nobody answers for a moment.

beats.title: Tomorrow Is My Choice
beats.screenAction: MC separates personal choice from political allegiance and chooses to return to the line because people will be left behind otherwise.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep MC's reason personal and consistent with the story so far; helping here does not mean swearing their life to France.
beats.result: MC chooses to fight at Tourelles while retaining the larger goal of answers and a route home.

script.text: I came here looking for a way home. Somehow I keep finding reasons not to leave people behind.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: That is not the same as owing France your life.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: No. Tomorrow is my choice.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: CH02-B03 — The Tourelles.

nodes.title: The Tourelles
nodes.summary: The siege climax. Jeanne is wounded, morale falters, and the objective shifts honestly to protecting the wounded and preventing collapse before she later returns visibly bandaged and the final assault resumes.

beats.title: The Wound
beats.screenAction: During the assault Jeanne is wounded and removed from the immediate line. The attack stalls as soldiers react to seeing her fall.
beats.dialogueIntent: Treat the wound as dangerous and frightening. No miraculous healing.
beats.result: The objective shifts from assault to hold/protect/reorganize while Jeanne is treated.

script.text: The assault compresses against the fortifications under heavy fire.
Jeanne jerks backward and falls among the front ranks.
Jeanne!
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Get her back! Now!
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: Hold Without Her
beats.screenAction: With Jeanne behind the line, the immediate goal becomes preventing collapse, protecting the treatment area, and keeping a route open.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make the objective shift mechanically and emotionally honest. MC does not replace Jeanne as commander or symbol.
beats.result: The French line survives the shock long enough to reorganize instead of collapsing.

script.text: Objective update: hold the line, protect the wounded, and prevent the assault from collapsing.
Nobody chases. Nobody panics. Hold what we have!
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: MC helps close a gap near the withdrawal route while Julie keeps the treatment lane clear.

beats.title: Bandaged Return
beats.screenAction: Jeanne later returns visibly bandaged. Her return restores morale enough for the final assault to resume; the battle is completed by the whole force.
beats.dialogueIntent: Preserve the approved wound → hold/protect → bandaged return flow without supernatural recovery or solo-protagonist replacement.
beats.result: The Tourelles falls and the siege reaches its breaking point.

script.text: A shout travels from the rear. Jeanne returns, pale and visibly bandaged, moving carefully but upright.
You are supposed to be lying down.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Later.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: Objective update: resume the final assault and secure the Tourelles.
The renewed assault finally breaks the position.
CH02-N08 — The Siege Is Lifted.

nodes.title: The Siege Is Lifted
nodes.summary: The English withdrawal resolves the siege. MC has no French rank and still wants a route home, but after the road, Cut Road, Saint-Loup, Augustins, and Tourelles, leaving the people here behind no longer feels simple.

beats.title: The English Leave
beats.screenAction: On 8 May the English withdrawal becomes visible. The city reacts with exhausted relief rather than a clean heroic tableau.
beats.dialogueIntent: Resolve the siege historically while keeping the human cost present.
beats.result: Orléans is no longer under the same siege pressure and the chapter's military objective is achieved.

script.text: By morning the English positions are emptying. People climb walls and roofs just to be certain.
They're leaving.
script.speaker: Civilian

script.text: Then let them leave before someone invents one more fight for today.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

beats.title: Useful Does Not Mean Finished
beats.screenAction: MC's party is now genuinely recognized after repeated local service and the major siege battles, but MC still has no formal rank and still wants answers about home.
beats.dialogueIntent: Close the chapter with earned reputation and an open personal goal rather than instant belonging.
beats.result: Chapter 2 ends with the party recognized as proven irregulars and the road toward the post-Orléans campaign opening.

script.text: People know us now. That still feels strange.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: They know what you did. That is different from knowing you.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

script.text: Good. I still have questions they cannot answer for me.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: CHAPTER 2 COMPLETE
Next: Chapter 3 — The Road to the Crown.

routeClusters.title: Proof Before Rank
routeClusters.summary: Three small local siege incidents are available in free order. Completing any two gives MC's party enough independent witnesses for Dunois to recognize them as useful irregulars; the third remains optional before the route reconverges.

nodes.title: Beyond Orléans
nodes.summary: After Orléans, MC does not simply attach to Jeanne. Dunois's report and the group's siege record give Alençon a practical reason to accept them with the Loire campaign as irregular veterans.

beats.title: A Place in the Column
beats.screenAction: Alençon reviews the people joining the Loire campaign. MC's group is accepted because Dunois and La Hire both report useful service, not because Jeanne personally grants status.
beats.dialogueIntent: Expand the political scale while making continued access causal and earned.
beats.result: MC chooses the next campaign leg and is accepted as an irregular veteran, still without formal rank.

script.text: The Orléans column is larger now: soldiers, carts, horses, engineers, and officers who have never met MC.
Dunois lists your group in the Saint-Loup, Augustins, and Tourelles reports.
script.speaker: Jean II d’Alençon

script.text: He makes us sound more organized than we are.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: La Hire makes you sound less organized.
script.speaker: Jean II d’Alençon

script.text: Also accurate.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: If you come, you follow the operation. No private war, no heroic wandering.
script.speaker: Jean II d’Alençon

script.text: Understood.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: CH03-B01 — Jargeau.

nodes.title: Jargeau
nodes.summary: The campaign attacks Jargeau. MC is one proven fighter among a larger army, while Suffolk anchors a serious English defense.

beats.title: Approach Jargeau
characters: William de la Pole, Earl of Suffolk
beats.screenAction: The assault begins against a prepared English defense. Alençon keeps the advance controlled while Suffolk tries to break French momentum.
beats.dialogueIntent: Establish Jargeau as a real campaign battle with command structure on both sides.
beats.result: The French reach the main defenses without turning the opening into a reckless rush.

script.text: Objective: reach the main defenses while keeping the assault line coherent.
They have momentum. Break it here.
script.speaker: William de la Pole, Earl of Suffolk

script.text: The French push through the outer defenses in successive waves rather than a single rush.

beats.title: Inside the Pressure
beats.screenAction: The assault becomes a sustained contest over breaches and streets. MC operates as one proven fighter among the forward groups.
beats.dialogueIntent: Avoid collapsing a whole siege assault into one line. Reputation now means dependable placement, not special command.
beats.result: French pressure reaches the point where organized English resistance can no longer hold every approach.

script.text: Keep the pressure. Do not outrun the line.
script.speaker: Jean II d’Alençon

script.text: Objective update: secure the breach and prevent the forward line from fragmenting.
MC's group rotates wounded fighters out while fresh soldiers press through the same opening.

beats.title: Suffolk Captured
characters: William de la Pole, Earl of Suffolk
beats.screenAction: Organized resistance collapses and Suffolk is captured. Victory immediately creates prisoners, wounded, and the next campaign problem.
beats.dialogueIntent: End the battle on consequences instead of treating capture as a boss trophy.
beats.result: Jargeau falls; Suffolk is captured; the campaign pauses long enough to process the result.

script.text: By the battle's end organized resistance collapses and Suffolk is taken prisoner.
Secure the prisoners. Find the wounded before the cheering gets in the way.
script.speaker: Jean II d’Alençon

script.text: CH03-N02 — After Jargeau.

nodes.title: After Jargeau
nodes.summary: The chapter stops to live with the victory. Prisoners are processed, wounded treated, and MC discovers that being recognized by more soldiers mostly means more people expect something next time.

beats.title: A Reputation Is Work
beats.screenAction: The field after Jargeau becomes lists, wounded, prisoners, supplies, and repairs. Recognition mostly means more people ask MC's group for help.
beats.dialogueIntent: Turn recognition into responsibility rather than protagonist privilege.
beats.result: MC sees reputation becoming ordinary work and expectation.

script.text: The field after Jargeau is full of lists: wounded, missing, prisoners, supplies, damaged equipment.
People keep congratulating us while handing us more things to carry.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: That is usually what a useful reputation becomes.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: {{MC_NAME}}. Your group stays with the forward column tomorrow.
script.speaker: Jean II d’Alençon

script.text: You remembered my name.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: You survived enough reports to earn that inconvenience.
script.speaker: Jean II d’Alençon

beats.title: Forward Column Tomorrow
beats.screenAction: Alençon now addresses the party without La Hire introducing them. A small disagreement over campaign pace follows while wounded are still being moved.
beats.dialogueIntent: Recognition is now believable because Orléans and Jargeau produced repeated firsthand evidence.
beats.result: Alençon personally knows the group and keeps them with the forward column; the next campaign leg begins with unresolved fatigue.

script.text: Jeanne looks toward the next road while the wounded are still being loaded.
We move again too soon.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Maybe. But the English are moving too.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: CH03-N03 — Between Fortresses.

nodes.title: Between Fortresses
nodes.summary: Meung and Beaugency are treated as a campaign transition rather than a teleport between headline battles. Richemont's arrival exposes political distrust inside the French side while field work continues.

beats.title: Pressure Without a Parade
beats.screenAction: The column pressures crossings, screens roads, moves supplies, and watches English positions around Meung and Beaugency without turning every contact into a full mandatory battle.
beats.dialogueIntent: Show campaign labor, scouting uncertainty, and smaller clashes between major set pieces.
beats.result: The French keep pressure on the English withdrawal and MC's group gains routine operational credibility.

script.text: For several days the war is bridges, dust, bad sleep, shouted warnings, and short fights that end before anyone can call them victories.
I think I preferred battles with names.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Those are only the ones people remember afterward.
script.speaker: Hangaku Gozen

beats.title: An Ally Nobody Invited
beats.screenAction: Richemont arrives with Breton strength. Officers react with distrust even while the campaign needs his soldiers.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make internal French politics visible through practical tension, not a lecture.
beats.result: Richemont's force is accepted for the immediate campaign, but MC understands that shared enemies do not erase internal conflict.

script.text: A fresh column approaches under Breton banners while nearby officers react with more suspicion than relief.
Those are ours, yes?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: That depends which argument you are asking about.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: Arthur de Richemont. I brought soldiers, not a debate.
script.speaker: Arthur de Richemont

script.text: For today, soldiers are useful.
script.speaker: Jean II d’Alençon

script.text: CH03-N04 — The Enemy Is Moving.

nodes.title: The Enemy Is Moving
nodes.summary: Before Patay, the army does not know it is walking into a famous victory. Scouts bring incomplete reports, commanders argue over speed, and La Hire's vanguard pushes to catch the English before they settle.

beats.title: Bad Information
beats.screenAction: Scouts bring conflicting positions for the withdrawing English. Nobody knows yet that Patay will become a famous victory.
beats.dialogueIntent: Create uncertainty before the decision to press.
beats.result: The commanders understand they have a narrow opportunity but incomplete information.

script.text: A scout arrives with dust on his face and three different estimates of where the English column is.
If we wait for perfect information, they build the line we do not want to attack.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: If we rush blind, we may find it anyway.
script.speaker: Jean II d’Alençon

script.text: So what do we actually know?
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: Before the Line Sets
beats.screenAction: La Hire argues that waiting guarantees a prepared English line. The vanguard moves to make contact while the rest follows cautiously.
beats.dialogueIntent: Make Patay causality explicit: the opportunity exists because the French catch the withdrawal before deployment stabilizes.
beats.result: La Hire's vanguard moves to make contact before the English position stabilizes.

script.text: They are moving. We are close. That is enough for the vanguard to look.
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: The mounted screen pushes ahead. The rest of the column follows without knowing whether the next hour is pursuit or battle.
CH03-B02 — Patay.

nodes.title: Patay
nodes.summary: The French catch the retreating English before their field position fully settles. Talbot remains formidable, but conditions and timing turn the battle.

beats.title: Contact Before Deployment
beats.screenAction: The French vanguard catches the retreating English before their field line is fully established.
beats.dialogueIntent: Patay begins as an opportunity created by timing, not as a guaranteed scripted victory.
beats.result: The French reach the incomplete position before Talbot can fully organize it.

script.text: Objective: strike before the English line fully forms.
Now! Do not give them time to plant themselves!
script.speaker: La Hire

script.text: Mounted French forces surge toward the incomplete position.

beats.title: The Line Breaks
beats.screenAction: Talbot tries to stabilize the defense while French pressure hits before the formation is ready.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep Talbot formidable even while circumstances turn sharply against him.
beats.result: The incomplete English formation breaks and the battle turns into collapse and capture.

script.text: Hold the line!
script.speaker: John Talbot

script.text: The formation breaks before it can become the defense Talbot wanted.
Objective update: prevent an organized withdrawal while preserving the French advance.

beats.title: Talbot Under Guard
beats.screenAction: Talbot is captured. He remains composed enough to warn that one badly timed defeat does not end the war.
beats.dialogueIntent: Give the battle an aftermath beat and preserve Talbot's weight as a future threat rather than a disposable boss.
beats.result: Patay ends with Talbot captured and the French campaign politically transformed, but not complete.

script.text: Talbot is brought under guard, furious but composed.
Do not mistake catching an army unready for the end of the war.
script.speaker: John Talbot

script.text: Nobody here looks like they think the war is over.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: CH03-N05 — The Road to Reims.

nodes.title: The Road to Reims
nodes.summary: The road north is political as much as military. Charles enters MC's orbit only in a public campaign setting after reports from Dunois and Alençon have made the irregular group known.

beats.title: After Patay
beats.screenAction: The army counts the cost of Patay and prepares to move again. MC's growing reputation is visible but not glamorous.
beats.dialogueIntent: Give another breath before the political road; show success creating expectation rather than privilege.
beats.result: MC understands that people now expect the group to be dependable by default.

script.text: Patay ends quickly. Cleaning up does not.
Someone just asked me where they should put prisoners. Why would I know that?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Because you keep looking like you will answer.
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: I need to stop doing that.
script.speaker: MC

beats.title: The King Before the Crown
beats.screenAction: During a group campaign halt, Alençon identifies veterans whose reports Charles has been reading. MC is one name among them, not the recipient of a private royal audience.
beats.dialogueIntent: Keep Charles cautious and human. His awareness of MC is earned through reports and repeated service.
beats.result: MC understands that Jeanne's next goal is public legitimacy at Reims and that Charles is still uncertain about the road.

script.text: At a campaign halt, Alençon summarizes the forward groups while Charles listens with more caution than ceremony.
The irregulars from Orléans are still with us. Dunois was right about them.
script.speaker: Jean II d’Alençon

script.text: So you are {{MC_NAME}}. Your name appears in an unreasonable number of reports for someone with no rank.
script.speaker: Charles VII

script.text: I have been told the lack of rank is a blessing.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: Often it is.
script.speaker: Charles VII

script.text: Jeanne says the road ends at Reims.
script.speaker: MC

script.text: If Reims receives us, the crown changes what people believe is possible. That is why every gate on this road matters.
script.speaker: Charles VII

script.text: The conversation ends when another messenger arrives. Charles returns to the larger campaign, not to MC.
CH03-N06 — The Crown at Reims.

nodes.title: The Crown at Reims
nodes.summary: Charles is crowned at Reims. The chapter closes on the apparent fulfillment of Jeanne's great public mission and a restrained suggestion that the world is not as settled as it should be.

beats.title: The Crown
beats.screenAction: The coronation unfolds amid heat, armor, cloth, incense, and accumulated campaign fatigue. MC is present with the campaign, not centered by the ceremony.
beats.dialogueIntent: Let the historical milestone land, then add one subtle Fracture-like visual clue without explanation.
beats.result: Chapter 3 ends with Charles crowned and a faint refractive-light anomaly pointing toward the saga's darker turn.

script.text: Reims — 17 July 1429
The cathedral is filled with ceremony, heat, armor, cloth, incense, and people trying not to miss history happening in front of them.
Charles receives the crown. The sound inside the cathedral swells.
So that is it?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: For this road.
script.speaker: Jeanne d’Arc

script.text: For a heartbeat, light bends strangely across a distant pane of glass. MC turns toward it.
Did you see that?
script.speaker: MC

script.text: See what?
script.speaker: Julie d’Aubigny

script.text: The light is normal again.
CHAPTER 3 COMPLETE
Next: Chapter 4 — The Maid Falls.
